stories.body: President Donald Trump rejected Iran's proposed seven-day roadmap to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and begin negotiations, calling its terms unacceptable. Iran says the plan would require the United States to release frozen Iranian assets, lift oil sanctions and end its naval blockade, after which Tehran would reopen the waterway and resume nuclear talks. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Iran is awaiting a definitive response through mediators and maintains that only a negotiated settlement can end the conflict. The strait, a vital route for global oil and gas shipments, has been effectively closed since the war began in February, contributing to higher energy prices.
stories.headline: Trump rejects Iran's proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: Police declared a major incident and evacuated homes in Whelford, Gloucestershire, after arresting several men on suspicion of explosives offences near RAF Fairford. Army explosive ordnance disposal specialists were examining several vehicles, while residents were taken to a nearby leisure centre and police imposed a cordon. Authorities said they believed the incident was contained but did not say whether explosives had been found or whether the case was connected to the nearby base, which has been used by US forces during operations related to Iran.
stories.headline: UK police arrest men and evacuate homes near RAF Fairford

stories.body: At least 27 people were killed and more than 25 wounded in two mass shootings in South African townships hours apart. Eight gunmen armed with rifles and pistols attacked a tavern in Wedela, southwest of Johannesburg, killing 17 people and injuring 15; police said the attackers also searched some patrons, took phones and set two vehicles alight. In Lwandle near Cape Town, gunmen killed 10 people and wounded 11 at an entertainment venue. No arrests had been announced, and investigators had not established motives as the attacks followed another mass shooting near Durban days earlier.
stories.headline: Two mass shootings in South Africa kill at least 27 people

stories.body: Russia and Ukraine continued to exchange drone and missile strikes, with authorities reporting at least 16 deaths over a 24-hour period. Russian attacks killed at least four people across Ukraine, while both countries have intensified long-range attacks on civilian and critical infrastructure. The United Nations has warned that the escalation is driving up civilian casualties as the war's aerial campaign expands.
stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine trade deadly long-range strikes

stories.body: A powerful nor'easter brought heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous coastal flooding to the northeastern United States, prompting emergency declarations in New York and New Jersey. More than 100,000 households lost power, thousands of flights were delayed or cancelled, and events from New York to Massachusetts were called off. A man in Brooklyn was reportedly killed by a falling tree, while coastal communities in New Jersey saw streets and homes inundated. Forecasters warned that a full moon could worsen tidal flooding, with hazardous conditions extending from Virginia to Maine.
stories.headline: Powerful nor'easter triggers flooding emergencies in New York and New Jersey

stories.body: Several US states are cutting or considering cuts to gasoline taxes as the war with Iran pushes fuel costs higher ahead of the midterm elections. Georgia, Kentucky and Indiana have reduced or suspended their fuel taxes, while Ohio and Massachusetts are weighing similar proposals. The measures are intended to offer consumers short-term relief as high fuel prices add to broader concerns about household affordability.
stories.headline: States consider gas-tax holidays as fuel prices rise

stories.body: A Politico poll found that voters who identify with the MAGA movement are substantially less likely than other Americans to say the cost of living has worsened since Donald Trump took office. Only 28% of MAGA voters said expenses had become less affordable, while non-MAGA Trump voters were more closely aligned with Democratic voters in their concerns. The findings suggest that affordability could strain the Republican coalition ahead of the midterms, particularly among Trump voters who do not identify with the MAGA movement and younger voters.
stories.headline: Poll finds Trump's MAGA base less worried about affordability

stories.body: The Department of Homeland Security says it plans to use artificial intelligence to help determine how records are redacted before they are released to the public. The agency has described the technology as a way to transform its redaction process, raising questions about the role automated systems could play in decisions affecting public access to government information.
stories.headline: Department of Homeland Security plans to use AI for public-record redactions

stories.body: The Supreme Court has blocked a Missouri congressional map that favored Republicans for a third time, ending a complex legal fight that had created uncertainty over the state's November midterm elections. The decision prevents the disputed map from taking effect while Missouri's congressional districts remain subject to continuing legal and electoral scrutiny.
stories.headline: Supreme Court again blocks Republican-favored Missouri congressional map

stories.body: Hundreds of people camped overnight in Madrid's Puerta del Sol after a large demonstration over the housing crisis and the eviction of an elderly tenant known as Maricarmen. Organised by the Madrid Tenants' Union, protesters are demanding that the government approve a housing decree that would include measures such as rent freezes, stronger protections against evictions and longer or indefinite rental contracts. Organisers said they would continue pressing the government ahead of a planned Cabinet meeting on Tuesday.
stories.headline: Hundreds camp in Madrid after housing protest

stories.body: The eviction of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old Madrid tenant who had lived in her home for about 70 years, has become a focal point in negotiations over new housing protections. According to reports, she had continued paying her old-rent lease and bills, but the apartment's owners sought her removal after purchasing the property in 2018. Her case has added public pressure on the government and its parliamentary partners to agree on an anti-eviction decree, although differences and mutual vetoes among the parties remain.
stories.headline: Eviction of 87-year-old Madrid tenant increases pressure for housing decree

stories.body: Spain's government is preparing an emergency decree intended to accelerate the return to Morocco of migrants who remain in Ceuta after a mass crossing on 30 July. The measure, reportedly being prepared for approval at Tuesday's Cabinet meeting, would apply to asylum applications registered in Ceuta since the crossing and shorten administrative and judicial deadlines. Separately, police dismantled a migrant encampment near Ceuta's desalination plant, relocating those affected while authorities cited security and safety concerns.
stories.headline: Spanish government prepares decree to speed migrant returns from Ceuta to Morocco

stories.body: Madrid investigating judge Juan Carlos Peinado retired on his 72nd birthday, days after ordering Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, to stand trial before a jury on alleged influence-peddling and embezzlement charges. Peinado's investigation of Gómez, which began in 2024, made him a deeply divisive public figure: critics, including members of the government, have alleged politically motivated lawfare, while supporters have defended his work. The Madrid provincial court will now determine the timing of any trial.
stories.headline: Judge who sent Pedro Sánchez's wife to trial retires

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court is expected to rule in early October on the application of the amnesty law to embezzlement convictions and allegations linked to Catalonia's independence process, a decision that could remove a major legal obstacle to Carles Puigdemont's return to Spain. The court's progressive majority has already indicated that it is unlikely to oppose applying the amnesty in such cases. Puigdemont, the former Catalan president who has remained abroad, is reportedly preparing for the possibility of returning if the ruling goes his way.
stories.headline: Constitutional Court ruling could clear way for Puigdemont's return to Spain

stories.body: Barcelona's La Mercè festival concludes on Sunday night with its traditional piromusical, relocated this year from Avinguda Maria Cristina to Nova Icària beach because of construction work at the Fira de Barcelona site. The half-hour show will combine synchronised fireworks and music selected by Josep Montero, singer of the Catalan group Oques Grasses. Public transport, especially Metro line L4 and several bus routes, is being reinforced for the event, which is expected to draw large crowds along the seafront.
stories.headline: La Mercè ends with piromusical at Nova Icària beach

stories.body: The Polytechnic University of Catalonia is testing two retractable, solar-powered pergolas at its North Campus as possible solutions for Barcelona's heavily paved public squares, where underground infrastructure often prevents tree planting. The year-long pilot will measure whether the structures reduce heat and improve comfort, while also assessing their durability and social use. One design uses photovoltaic panels and a breathable catalytic canopy intended to help filter pollutants, while the other combines fixed solar panels with retractable wooden slats that can provide shade in summer and admit sunlight in winter.
stories.headline: University tests retractable solar pergolas for Barcelona's heat-prone squares

stories.body: Surface sea temperatures along Catalonia's coast reached an average of 26.1C during the summer, 2.3C above the 1982-2022 average and the highest seasonal figure in the available record, according to data cited from the Catalan Institute for Research on Marine Governance. July averaged 27C and August 28.4C, both record monthly readings, while June was the second-warmest June since 1982. The figures underscore the persistence and intensity of the marine heat experienced off the Catalan coast this year.
stories.headline: Catalan coastal sea temperatures break summer records
